Milk streams off the sides of her fingers in thin falling threads into the soft white blur of the paraat below; no milk drop, drip or bead touches the earrings or any stone, only a faint wet sheen on the metal. A light shower of small blush and ivory rose petals falls through the frame from above, frozen by the flash like ticker-tape, each petal small and none in front of the earrings. Background: deep oxblood velvet shamiana drape in soft vertical folds, far out of focus, with a few small warm fairy-light discs. PLACEMENT: the earrings sit centred left to right, between 35% and 47% of the way down the frame. Above them, the top third is calm dark oxblood with at most two petals, for the headline: the same velvet continuing up to the top edge in soft dark folds with real fabric texture. Below her fingers, dark oxblood and the falling milk threads fill 50-68% for the price card, and the lowest third is the soft out-of-focus brass paraat rim and the milk crown falling back, with no petals. LIGHT: two lights only: a soft warm key from the left; one small hard specular kicker from behind right puts one white catchlight in each clear pear and lights the mint pear from within. Natural film grain, editorial demi-fine jewellery campaign quality. Only one hand: no face, no eyes, no eyebrows, no head. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermark anywhere, nothing written in the mehendi. One product only: this one pair of earrings is the only jewellery in the frame; no star glints, no rainbow flare.
